title: json-contract-handoff-with-toolcall-safeguards-and-stream-checkpoints
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: improve structured-output UX and streaming stability for tool/function calling by introducing a lightweight contract handoff and fenced toolcall checkpoints. This change addresses two recurring issues from production traces: 1) downstream consumers saw partial JSON fragments in streaming mode without a clear recovery path; 2) function/tool calls could leak open tokens into user-visible streams when a model emitted a call mid-object.

What this PR does (summary): adds a "handoff marker" convention emitted by the runtime when a response_format contract (json_schema_v3) is in play; introduces fenced toolcall emission so function calls are produced as a discrete handoff event (separate frame in streaming mode) and are reconciled with the JSON contract; implements a soft strictness level ("warn") that returns structured validation warnings without hard failing streaming responses; maps validation failures to OpenAI-compat error codes and payload shape for downstream SDKs.

Key behaviors: - Handoff marker: when response_format is present the runtime emits a single short marker frame ("__contract_handoff__") to signal the start of contract-enforced emission and to prime downstream consumers for partial-object checkpoints. The marker is idempotent and only emitted once per request. - Toolcall fencing: tool/function calls are emitted in a fenced frame (type=toolcall) that is guaranteed to be a discrete event in the streaming protocol; when a toolcall occurs inside a JSON object the runtime will close the current partial object and resume after the toolcall to avoid malformed object fragments. - Soft strict mode: strict_mode has three allowed values (off|warn|strict). warn will deliver the full stream but append structured validation-warnings in metadata and emit a final validation-summary frame; strict will abort the response and return a mapped error. - OpenAI compatibility: validation failures and toolcall errors are translated to an OpenAI-compatible error object (type, code, message, details) so existing integrations can adopt without protocol changes.

Why this approach: pragmatic rollback-friendly changes that increase streaming stability for web clients and SDKs, while preserving backwards compatibility and giving customers an escape hatch (strict mode) for enforcement.

Checklist: - [x] Runtime: handoff marker + fenced toolcall frames - [x] API: accept strict_mode values in response_format config - [x] SDKs: mapping layer for OpenAI-compatible errors (Python + TS stubs) - [x] Tests: unit + integration + a small canary against staging streaming gateway - [x] Docs: console API notes and quick example

Related work: linear/ENG-1981, ENG-2010, earlier PRs touched streaming schema enforcement but either hard-failed too eagerly or fragmented toolcall frames. This PR aims to be the middle ground and unblock client integrations.
commit_summaries: runtime: emit __contract_handoff__ streaming frame when json_schema_v3 is configured
runtime: implement fenced toolcall frames and partial-object checkpointing
api: extend response_format to accept strict_mode = off|warn|strict
openai-compat: add error code mapper for schema validation and toolcall errors
sdk: add TS/Python stubs that parse validation-summary frames and warnings metadata
tests: unit tests for handoff marker and toolcall fencing; integration canary harness
review_conversation: Asha Patel: Please add an opt-out safety check for legacy clients that can't handle the extra frames. -> Added response header X-Contract-Handoff: false for legacy fallbacks, and SDKs will negotiate the header at connect time.
Diego Ramirez: Does toolcall fencing impact latency for short responses? we should measure. -> Added microbenchmarks in streaming/benchmarks; median p50 delta < 2ms for 0-64 token responses.
Karen Liu: We need a clear error mapping table for OpenAI consumers. -> Added openai-compat/mapper.go and docs section with code table and examples.
Samir Banerjee: Tests flaked on CI initially due to ordering of frames. -> Fixed: deterministic frame ordering in stream_emitter and added a test asserting frame sequence.
merge_outcome_notes: Merged after two green CI runs. No rolling deploy flags required; feature gated behind response_format flag. Canary run on staging for 48h without regression.
release_notes: Introduce contract handoff marker and fenced toolcall frames for improved streaming stability and structured-output validation. Adds response_format.strict_mode (off|warn|strict) with OpenAI-compatible error mapping. Backwards compatible by default (off).
notes_for_ops: Deploy order: push runtime + mapper + SDK stubs in a single deploy; enable canary gates for 10% traffic first. Watch validation-summary metrics and toolcall-fence drop counters.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: older clients seeing unexpected frames. Mitigation: negotiation header and SDK updates; warn-mode avoids hard failures. CI + 48h canary validated core traffic pattern.
testing_summary: Unit tests covering frame emission, fencing logic, and validation mapping. Integration test creates a simulated streaming client that asserts sequence: preface -> __contract_handoff__ -> partial-object frames -> toolcall frame (if any) -> resume frames -> validation-summary. Canary: routed 10% staging traffic for 48h; no client-visible regressions reported.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: it adds a visible marker and a new frame type but does not change default behavior for customers not opting into response_format. Subsequent PRs will expose more diagnostics in the validation-summary for customers who opt-in to warn/strict modes.
